title: Simple Harmonic Motion
learning_goal: Examine simple harmonic motion and wave-energy propagation using springs, pendulums, and related systems.

stages.title: 1. Repeating motion
stages.content: Simple harmonic motion is repetitive motion around an equilibrium position caused by a restoring force. Springs and small-angle pendulums are common examples.

stages.title: 2. Equilibrium and restoring force
stages.content: At equilibrium, the system has no displacement from its balance position. When displaced, a restoring force acts toward equilibrium.

stages.title: 3. Energy changes during oscillation
stages.content: In an ideal oscillator, energy continually transforms between kinetic energy and potential energy while total mechanical energy remains constant.

stages.title: 4. Worked example
stages.content: A mass on a spring moves fastest as it passes equilibrium because potential energy is lowest and kinetic energy is highest there.

stages.title: 5. Guided practice
stages.prompt: At the maximum displacement of a mass on a spring, is its speed maximum or minimum?
stages.hint: Think about what happens at the turning point before the mass reverses direction.
stages.alternate_explanation: At the extreme position the mass pauses momentarily, so kinetic energy is smallest there.
stages.answer: Its speed is minimum, momentarily zero.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, identify equilibrium, describe restoring force, compare kinetic and potential energy during oscillation, and connect oscillations to wave-energy propagation.

concept_cards.title: Repeating motion
concept_cards.content: Simple harmonic motion is repetitive motion around an equilibrium position caused by a restoring force. Springs and small-angle pendulums are common examples.

visual.label: At extremes speed is zero; at equilibrium speed is greatest for an ideal oscillator.

concept_cards.title: Equilibrium and restoring force
concept_cards.content: At equilibrium, the system has no displacement from its balance position. When displaced, a restoring force acts toward equilibrium.

concept_cards.title: Energy changes during oscillation
concept_cards.content: In an ideal oscillator, energy continually transforms between kinetic energy and potential energy while total mechanical energy remains constant.

concept_cards.title: What defines an ideal simple harmonic restoring force?
concept_cards.content: F = −kx gives acceleration a = −(k/m)x. The negative sign means the force points toward equilibrium.

concept_cards.title: At the extreme displacement of an ideal mass-spring oscillator, what is its speed?
concept_cards.content: The mass reverses direction there. Spring potential energy is maximum and kinetic energy is zero; restoring acceleration is greatest in magnitude.
